description:
I am a young space enthusiast with a strong interest in space exploration, astronomy, science, technology, and game development. I am particularly interested in NASA's missions and the stories behind abandoned scientific equipment on the Moon and Mars. 

I welcome people who are enthusiastic, willing to learn, share ideas, and collaborate. Together, we can transform scientific discoveries into an exciting experience that inspires more people to explore and understand our universe.
summary:
This video is about NASA's equipment that was left behind on the Moon and Mars after their missions. It shows how these machines played an important role in space exploration.

On the Moon, astronauts left behind lunar rovers, scientific instruments and other equipment during the Apollo missions. Some of these instruments continued collecting useful information even after the astronauts returned to Earth.

The video also introduces NASA's Mars rovers, including Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity. These rovers explored the surface of Mars, studied rocks and helped scientists discover evidence of ancient water.

Overall, this video reminds us that even though some machines are no longer working or have been left behind, their discoveries and contributions are still important. They helped us learn more about the Moon and Mars and inspired future space exploration.
details:
Our project, “DONE BUT NOT FORGOTTEN,” is a creative digital documentary that explores the forgotten equipment and machines left behind during space exploration, especially on the Moon and Mars. It highlights how these machines, although no longer actively used, have played an important role in helping humans understand space and discover more about other worlds.

The main purpose of our project is to raise awareness of the importance of past space missions and show that every piece of equipment has its own story and contribution to science. From Apollo equipment on the Moon to NASA’s robotic explorers on Mars, we bring attention to the history, discoveries and achievements behind these forgotten machines.

Our project is designed to present information through an engaging visual storytelling experience. We combine creative backgrounds, space-themed illustrations, planets, animations and informative text to make the documentary more interesting, attractive and easier to understand. We use digital design and video-editing tools to develop our presentation and bring our ideas to life.

What makes our project unique is its storytelling approach. Instead of focusing only on successful space missions, we explore what happens after a mission ends and the equipment is left behind. We want our audience to see that even when a mission is over, its contributions to science and future exploration are never forgotten.

We also considered the accuracy of information, creativity, visual presentation and educational value when developing our project. Through this project, we hope to inspire people, especially young learners, to appreciate space exploration, understand NASA’s achievements and become more interested in science and technology. Our message is simple: Missions end, but their stories live on.
